rdf:Description.rdfs:label: deployed
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SBOM provides an inventory of software that is present on a system. This may be an assembly of other SBOMs that combines analysis of configuration options, and examination of execution behavior in a (potentially simulated) deployment environment.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: sha256
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SHA-2 with a digest length of 256, as defined in [RFC 6234](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc6234/).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: notAutomated
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Level 0 - Not automated. No automation. The operator fully controls the system.

RequirementVerification class defines the base properties of a verification.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: componentNotPresent
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The software is not affected because the vulnerable component is not in the product.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: runtime
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SBOM generated through instrumenting the system running the software, to capture only components present in the system, as well as external call-outs or dynamically loaded components. In some contexts, this may also be referred to as an "Instrumented" or "Dynamic" SBOM.
QUDT unit is used for measurement criteria based on product type, region and use.
Specifies a country code of the location.
Preprocessing steps applied to the training data before the model training.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: follows
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `to` Element succeeds the `from` Element, establishing a unidirectional sequence. This succession is defined as chronological, procedural, or logical. It is used to represent either a temporal order (e.g., in a workflow) or a logical order for processing and traversal (e.g., in an ordered list).
Products out of specification require a resolution action. This is the action of resolution.
A text describing the design constraint defined by the assumption.
Maps a "LicenseRef-" string for a custom license or a "AdditionRef-" string for a custom license addition to a `CustomLicense`, a `CustomLicenseAddition`, or a `SimpleLicensingText`.
A buildId is a locally unique identifier used by a builder to identify a unique instance of a build produced by it.
A verificationUUID is a universally unique identifier (UUID) assigned to a Verification item.
A specification type defines the nature of a specification.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: review
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Used when someone reviews the Element.
A class for describing the energy consumption incurred by an AI model in different stages of its lifecycle.
Class that describes an InstantiateVirtualHardwareProcess that is used to define VirtualHardware and its source.
The DefinedType class associates a specific type with its defined source.
A Package that contains AI software or an AI model.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: lei
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The [Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)](https://www.gleif.org/en/organizational-identity/introducing-the-legal-entity-identifier-lei) is a 20-character, alphanumeric code based on the [ISO 17442](https://www.iso.org/standard/78829.html) standard developed by the International Organization for Standardization.
A license that is listed on the SPDX License List.
Abstract ancestor class for all vulnerability assessments.
Specifies the CVSS qualitative severity rating of a vulnerability in relation to a piece of software.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: source
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SBOM created directly from the development environment, source files, and included dependencies used to build a product artifact.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: query

Reproduction is the biological process by which living organisms produce offspring.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: observation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Documentation of direct monitoring or witnessing of the demonstration of processes, tests, or any kind of system responses during a specified timeframe under specified environmental conditions.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: fullAutomation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Level 5 - Full automation. The system is capable of performing its entire mission without external intervention.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: phoneNumber

A specification is a detailed description of the design, requirements, or features of a product, process, or system.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: swhid
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SoftWare Hash IDentifier, a persistent intrinsic identifier for digital artifacts, such as files, trees (also known as directories or folders), commits, and other objects typically found in version control systems. The format of the identifiers is defined in the [SWHID specification](https://www.swhid.org/swhid-specification/v1.2/) ([ISO/IEC 18670](https://www.iso.org/standard/89985.html)). They typically look like `swh:1:cnt:94a9ed024d3859793618152ea559a168bbcbb5e2`.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hsCodes

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: noAssertion

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: ownership
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Ownership refers to the legal right to control, manage, and benefit from an asset, resource, or responsibility. It establishes authority, accountability, and entitlements over something, whether it's property, a business, intellectual property, or responsibilities.

Limitation of the AI software.

Class that describes a process.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: expandsTo

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: documentation

A key with an Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: verificationUUID

An Element an annotator has made an assertion about.
Type of data in a dataset.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: evidenceUUID
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The UUID used by a reporting management system or any other lifecycle management tool to uniquely identify an evidence relationship item. UUID, or universally unique ID, is a standard term to refer to evidence items.
Information related to hardware dimension.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: decommission

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Designates a `from` Vulnerability was first reported to a project, vendor, or tracking database for formal identification by each `to` Agent.

A place for the SPDX document creator to record a website that serves as the package's home page.
The point in time when an element or an action ends, becomes no longer applicable, or becomes no longer valid.
A reference to a resource identifier defined outside the scope of SPDX 3 content that uniquely identifies an Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Every `to` Element is related to the `from` Element where the relationship type is not described by any of the SPDX relationship types (this relationship is directionless).
Specifies the exploit catalog type.
Portion of an AnyLicenseInfo representing a set of licensing information where only one of the elements applies.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: patch
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element contains a set of changes to update, fix, or improve another Element.
A name used in a CdxPropertyEntry name-value pair.
Specifies the type of an external identifier.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: specification
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A specification is a detailed document (or set of documents) that describes the requirements, design, behavior, or other characteristics of a system, component, or process so that all stakeholders have a clear, unambiguous reference.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: releaseNotes
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to the release notes for a package.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: audio
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Data is audio based, such as a collection of music from the 80s.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: endOfSupport
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: There is a defined end of support for the artifact from the supplier. This may also be referred to as end of life. There is a validUntilDate that can be used to signal when support ends for the artifact.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: ocsp
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Online Certificate Status Protocol, or OCSP, is a common scheme used to maintain the security of a server and other network resources.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: isbn
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: [International Standard Book Number (ISBN)](https://www.isbn-international.org/content/isbn-users-manual/29) is a unique numeric identifier for monographic publications standardized by [ISO 2108](https://www.iso.org/standard/65483.html). It consists of either 10 digits (for assignments prior to January 1, 2007) or 13 digits. A 13-digit ISBN is composed of five parts: a GS1 prefix, a registration group, a registrant, a publication element, and a check digit. While elements may be divided by spaces or hyphens for human readability, these separators shall be omitted when the identifier is stored electronically (e.g., `9780198836063`).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hasVariant
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Every `to` Element is a variant the `from` Element (`from` hasVariant `to`).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: attend
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The vulnerability requires attention from the organization's internal, supervisory-level individuals. Necessary actions include requesting assistance or information about the vulnerability, and may involve publishing a notification either internally and/or externally. CISA recommends remediating Attend vulnerabilities sooner than standard update timelines.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: custody

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SBOM generated through analysis of artifacts (e.g., executables, packages, containers, and virtual machine images) after its build. Such analysis generally requires a variety of heuristics. In some contexts, this may also be referred to as a "3rd party" SBOM.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: iscc
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: [International Standard Content Code (ISCC)](https://iscc.io/) is a content-derived identifier standardized by [ISO 24138](https://www.iso.org/standard/77899.html) for identifying digital assets. An ISCC-CODE typically look like `ISCC:KACT4EBWK27737D2AYCJRAL5Z36G76RFRMO4554RU26HZ4ORJGIVHDI`.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: diskImage
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element refers to a disk image that can be written to a disk, booted in a VM, etc. A disk image typically contains most or all of the components necessary to boot, such as bootloaders, kernels, firmware, userspace, etc.
